newsitem.title: USA: Dow falls as rate fears dominate choppy session.
newsitem.headline: Dow falls as rate fears dominate choppy session.

text.p: Wall Street stocks ended broadly lower on Tuesday, as a surprisingly strong report on the U.S. housing market reignited fears on Wall Street about inflation and interest rates.
The report jolted a market that analysts said is showing an extreme level of worry ahead of next week's Federal Reserve interest rate policy meeting.
The Dow industrials fell 59 points to close unofficially at 6897 after a volatile session that saw the average fall more than 100 points before recovering in the last minutes.

At the heart of the decline, said analysts, was news that new home building surged in February at the fastest pace in nearly three years, rising 12.2 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.53 million units.
While the increase was aided by unusually warm weather, the robust activity still surprised economists.
"Even adjusting for seasonal flukiness, the housing sector is doing extremely well," said David Wyss, an economist at DRI/McGraw Hill Inc.
Analysts said the news delivered a direct blow to a market already fixated on the Fed meeting.
"This market is obsessed with March 25," said Jack Shaughnessy, director of research at Advest. "The strong housing numbers this morning contributed to that."

Shaughnessy said the market appears prepared for a marginal increase of 25 basis points in short-term interest rates at the Fed meeting next week, but "there's a fear there might be even more of an increase."
With the meeting still a week away and several major events to come in the intervening sessions, analysts said volatility was only going to increase in the days ahead.

"We've got the (Consumer Price Index) tomorrow, triple witching on Friday and the Fed next week," said Alfred Goldman, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards and Sons. "Until the Fed drops the other shoe or puts it back on its foot, this market is going to stay whippy."

Banking shares were among the hardest hit by the rate jitters, with J.P. Morgan & Co Inc off 3-3/8 to 105, the steepest decline among Dow components. Chase Manhattan Corp fell 3-1/4 to 99-1/2 and Wells Fargo and Co dipped 5-3/4 to 297-1/8.
In individual issues, Wolverine Tube Inc fell 7-7/8 to 26 following the company's warning late on Monday that first quarter profits would be below year-ago levels.
Harman International Industries Inc skidded 11-3/4 to 34-1/4 on the heels of the company's warning that fiscal third quarter earnings would fall sharply versus last year.

Zenith Electric Corp jumped 2-1/2 to 12 on news that Time Warner Inc's cable television unit would use Zenith's set-top boxes as part of a service enhancement in some of its markets. Time Warner rose 1/2 to 43-1/2.
The S&P 500 index fell 6.05 points to 789.66.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 10.09 points to 1269.34.
